cgu_meta_desc: Terms of use and privacy policy of MiGallery, the photo library of the MiTV association: controller, legal bases, retention, rights.
cgu_subtitle: MiGallery - the MiTV association photo library
cgu_s1_intro: For a proper understanding of these terms:
cgu_s1_service: The Service: the MiGallery application and its API.
cgu_s1_user: The User: anyone with a MiConnect account giving access to MiGallery, that is, a member of the École des Mines de Saint-Étienne (EMSE).
cgu_s1_miconnect: MiConnect: the single sign-on service (OIDC) used to sign in to MiGallery and the association's other services.
cgu_s1_immich: Immich: the open-source software that stores and analyses the photos, installed on the MiGallery server.
cgu_s2_body: The data controller is the association MiTV (Mines TV), Maison des Élèves, 20 Boulevard Alexandre de Fraissinette, 42100 Saint-Étienne, France. For any question or request: bureau@mitv.fr.
cgu_s3_auth_body: You sign in through MiConnect. MiGallery never sees a password: it receives from MiConnect an identifier, your last name, first name, class year and programme.
cgu_s3_hosting_body: The photos and the database are on a server of the MiTV association; no photo is stored with a cloud provider. Three technical parties are worth knowing: MiConnect, the sign-in service, which is separate from MiGallery and whose hosting is covered by its own terms; Cloudflare, through which connections to the site pass (it relays the traffic, so it sees IP addresses and the exchanges while they transit; we entrust it with no storage); and the Canari project's server, on the same local network, which receives the backup copies (see retention).
cgu_s3_recipients_body: Your profile photo may be shown in other services of the association and the School (Canari, Sky, MinoWiki, Archives des Mines). API keys (machine credentials issued by an administrator) read face-linked photo sets, as administrators do. An unlisted album is open to anyone who has its link, and album cover images are public, private albums included. No data is sold or used for advertising.
cgu_s3_avail_body: The Service is provided "as is". Interruptions for maintenance or outages may occur.
cgu_s4_intro: Face recognition processes biometric data, a special category of data. Its legal basis is your explicit consent (GDPR article 9.2.a): you are free to refuse or withdraw it, and the rest of the Service keeps working.
cgu_s4_store: For every photo, with no action on your part: each face detected in a photo of the library (buffalo_l model) is turned into a digital face print: a series of numbers computed by a mathematical model, not a picture. MiGallery keeps one encrypted print for every face of the library, member or not. These prints carry no name and are not grouped by person: a face is tied to someone only by comparing it with the references of a member who agreed (see below). One exception, once only, when this design is put in place: the faces Immich had already linked to a member's account are grouped just long enough to compute that member's references (a working list and an average of those faces, both erased at the end of that step). The analysis runs on the same server as the photos, by Immich's analysis service, which MiGallery reaches over an internal network reserved to the two of them; no outside provider is involved. This processing concerns anyone appearing in a photo, member or not: to object, write to us (see Your rights).
cgu_s4_init: Your agreement and your references: you turn recognition on yourself, in the settings, by ticking the agreement box and then taking a selfie. Its print becomes your first reference, and MiGallery records the date, the version of these terms and how you agreed (selfie). A face you confirm afterwards may become a reference too, only when it closely resembles a reference you already hold: a face confirmed with a weaker resemblance enters "My Photos" but is never used as a reference. You hold at most 15 references, chosen to be varied (different angles, lights, ages) rather than alike; once you hold 15, a new reference replaces the most redundant one, keeping the more recent of the two by the photos' capture date, so that your references follow your face over time. Your selfie always stays a reference. Photos the comparison already gave you with a very strong resemblance may also serve as references, under the same rule. If your account was already linked to an Immich face group (the former design, see below), your references were taken among the faces of that group, so from your own photos, and only if you had not withdrawn; the origin recorded at the time is kept until your first selfie, whose agreement replaces it (selfie, administrator, or legacy for links made before this record existed, collected by another means).
cgu_s4_selfie: The selfie: the server analyses it in memory and then forgets it; it is never stored, neither in MiGallery nor in Immich. Only its print is kept. A selfie showing more than one face is refused, and nothing of it is kept.
cgu_s4_match: How your photos are found: every face of the library is compared with the references of the members who agreed, and can go to one member only, the one it resembles most. When the resemblance is strong, the photo goes straight into "My Photos". When it is weaker, when another member resembles it almost as much, or while you hold fewer than 3 references, the face is first offered to you on a confirmation screen, with a picture of the face cut out for you alone: it enters "My Photos" only if you answer "It's me"; "Not me" sets it aside, it is never offered to you again and may go to another member; its print is kept, encrypted, as a negative example for you alone (at most 30): a face that resembles it more than your references is no longer offered to you. Your negative examples change nothing for other members. A photo that entered "My Photos" stays there: a new comparison may add photos for you, never take one away; only your "Not me", or another member confirming that face, takes it out. Mistakes remain possible: a photo that is not of you may be shown or offered to you.
cgu_s4_cutover: The former design: until now, Immich itself grouped faces into anonymous groups, and a member linked a group to their account. MiGallery no longer uses those groups. At the cutover to the design described here, they are deleted from Immich, with their faces and prints; an encrypted copy of what is deleted is kept for 30 days, then deleted.
cgu_s4_myphotos_body: "My Photos" is visible to you, to the library administrators and to the people you open it to. The faces offered to you, and their cut-out pictures, are shown to you alone.
cgu_s4_spectator: Spectator mode: you may allow other users to see your identified photos. This is your choice and can be revoked at any time.
cgu_s4_revoke_body: You can withdraw in Settings → Danger zone, or by deleting your account. Immediately, MiGallery deletes your references, your negative examples, the list of photos given to you and your answers, the face pictures cut out for you, your profile photo and the sharing permissions you had given; the record of your agreement is closed with the date of the withdrawal. The faces that were given to you may then go to another member who resembles them. Withdrawal does not touch the prints of all the faces of the library, yours included: with no name and no reference, they are tied to nobody, and they go with their photo (to have a photo removed, write to us). Until the cutover, MiGallery also erases your name on the anonymous Immich group that was linked to your account. Backups keep the previous state until they rotate out (see below).
cgu_s5_items_title: Which data, what for, on what basis
cgu_s5_item_account: Account (identifier, last name, first name, class year, programme, role, language, favourites): to recognise you and manage access. Basis: performance of the service you request.
cgu_s5_item_photos: Student-life photos: to archive them and show them to members. Basis: the association's legitimate interest in keeping the memory of life at the School; you may object, or ask for a photo to be blurred or deleted (see Your rights).
cgu_s5_item_face: Your face (your references, your negative examples, the photos given to you and your answers, the face pictures cut out for you, your profile photo, the consent record): the "My Photos" feature. Basis: your explicit consent.
cgu_s5_item_store: Prints of every face of the library (one per detected face, member or not, encrypted, with no name): finding the photos of the members who asked for it (see section 4).
cgu_s5_item_logs: Technical logs (action, date, IP address): security and traceability of administration actions. Basis: the legitimate interest in protecting the Service.
cgu_s5_retention_photos: Photos: without time limit, for historical and heritage purposes, unless an erasure request removes them.
cgu_s5_retention_account: Account, favourites, consent record: as long as your account exists, deleted with it. A withdrawal keeps the record of the withdrawal (date, version) until the account is deleted.
cgu_s5_retention_face: Your references, the photos given to you, your answers, the pictures cut out for you: until you withdraw or delete your account.
cgu_s5_retention_store: Prints of the faces of the library: as long as the photo exists. A photo placed in Immich's trash still exists (it can be restored from there): its prints are kept until the trash is emptied. Once the photo is really deleted, its prints are erased when two checks of the library, at least 20 hours apart, have both found it missing; in practice, within the following days.
cgu_s5_retention_logs: Logs: 90 days at most. When an account is deleted, its identifier is removed from the logs we keep, along with the IP address of the actions it performed.
cgu_s5_backups_title: Backups: an erasure does not reach them at once
cgu_s5_backups_body: A deletion or a withdrawal of consent stays visible in backups until they rotate out. The last 10 daily copies of the MiGallery database on the server, and its copies on the Canari project's server (about 14 days), hold your references, the photos given to you and your answers. The Immich database copies (about 7 days, plus Immich's own local backups, whose duration is an Immich setting) taken before the cutover hold Immich's former face groups, and keep them until those copies rotate out; the encrypted copy made at the cutover is deleted after 30 days. The prints of all the faces of the library are in no backup: if they are lost, they are computed again from the photos. These copies are not consulted day to day and only serve to restore the service.
cgu_s6_intro: You may ask for access to your data, its rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and portability, withdraw your consent at any time, and object to processing based on legitimate interest (photos, logs).
cgu_s6_how: Write to bureau@mitv.fr: we reply within one month. Withdrawing consent to face recognition and deleting your account can also be done yourself in the settings.
cgu_s6_cnil: If you believe your rights are not respected, you may lodge a complaint with the CNIL (cnil.fr).
cgu_s7_body: The Service is reserved for members of the School. In France a minor may consent alone to the processing of their data from the age of 15; below that, the agreement of a holder of parental authority is required, which MiGallery cannot collect. Do not enable face recognition if you are under 15.
cgu_s8_body1: Only MiTV members may upload albums. The association keeps the exploitation rights.
cgu_s8_body2: Scraping the content, using it commercially, or tricking the face recognition system is forbidden.
